newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Australia, Malaysia plan closer ties.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Malaysia plan closer ties.

text.p: Australia and Malaysia, which have had a fractious relationship at times, have agreed to four cooperative measures including plans for regular ministerial talks, Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Sunday.
Australia already holds such talks with Thailand and Singapore, Downer said. Details of its plan to include Malaysia in such discussions would be worked out in the next few weeks, he said.

"Whether they will be annually or whether they will be bi-annually is one of the details we'll need to work out," he said. "But this does represent a significant upgrading of the political relationship between Australia and Malaysia," he added.

Downer was in Kuala Lumpur for meetings of the ASEAN Regional Forum, the main security forum for the region, following the annual ministerial meeting of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
The Australian minister's visit to Malaysia coincides with a fresh incident that threatened to sour relations between the two countries.

As he touched down here on Friday, Downer faced a barrage of questions about a secret Australia government report that said some Malaysian timber firms had helped support rulers in South Pacific countries.
Downer has played down the report, saying it was not an issue between the two governments.

Australia and Malaysia have sparred in the past over unflattering characterisations of Malaysia. Kuala Lumpur almost launched a trade war after then Australian Prime Minister Paul Keating called Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad a "recalcitrant" in late 1993.
Concerns about anti-Asian sentiment in Australia -- fuelled by race row politician Pauline Hanson -- have also frayed ties.
Downer said the other new links are increased cooperation in sports administration and information technology and a planned end to double taxation.
The cooperation in sports administration relates to Malaysia's hosting of the Commonwealth Games in 1998 and Australia playing host to the 2000 Olympics.
The information technology linkages will involve Australia's expertise in the field and Malaysia's plan for the high-tech Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) zone, Downer said.
Double taxation "has been a problem for Australian and Malaysian companies over the years", Downer said.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and as of Wednesday, new members Laos and Burma.
